## Big idea in one line

Three separate knobs:

1. **Cascade** — if I persist/delete parent, should children follow?  
2. **Fetch type** — load related data now or later?  
3. **Fetch plan per query** — for *this* use case, what graph do I need? (EntityGraph / join fetch)

```text
Cascade  ≠  ownership (mappedBy / JoinColumn)
Lazy     ≠  "never load"
EAGER    ≠  guaranteed single JOIN SQL
```

***

## Topic 1 — Cascading

Cascade = propagate a persistence operation along a relationship.

```java
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.PERSIST)
private List<OrderItem> items = new ArrayList<>();
```

```java
order.addItem(item1);
order.addItem(item2);
em.persist(order); // also persists item1, item2 if PERSIST cascade
```

### Cascade types

| Type | Propagates |
|------|------------|
| `PERSIST` | persist |
| `MERGE` | merge |
| `REMOVE` | remove |
| `REFRESH` | refresh |
| `DETACH` | detach |
| `ALL` | all of the above |

**Not on by default.** Add only when lifecycles truly belong together (order + order lines). Avoid `REMOVE` on shared many-to-many (deleting a student must not delete a shared course).

Helper still required for owning side:

```java
public void addItem(OrderItem item) {
    items.add(item);
    item.setOrder(this);
}
```

***

## Topic 2 — Lazy vs Eager

| Fetch | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `LAZY` | Load association when first needed (hint) |
| `EAGER` | Association must be available when entity is loaded |

### JPA defaults

| Relationship | Default |
|--------------|---------|
| `@ManyToOne` / `@OneToOne` | **EAGER** |
| `@OneToMany` / `@ManyToMany` | **LAZY** |

Practical habit: make to-one **LAZY** too, then fetch explicitly per use case.

```java
@ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
@JoinColumn(name = "department_id")
private Department department;
```

```text
find(Student)
  SELECT student columns...
  department = proxy (not loaded)

student.getDepartment().getName()
  SELECT department...   ← triggered now
```

***

## Topic 3 — N+1 problem

Pattern:

1. **1** query loads N parents  
2. Loop touches a lazy association → up to **N** more queries  

```java
List<Student> students = // findAll students
for (Student s : students) {
    System.out.println(s.getDepartment().getName()); // may query each time
}
```

```text
SELECT * FROM student;                 -- 1
SELECT * FROM department WHERE id=?;   -- +1 per distinct miss
...
```

L1 cache can reduce duplicates (100 students, 3 departments → maybe 1+3), but the design smell remains: relationship access hides SQL.

Same idea for collections:

```text
SELECT * FROM department;                      -- 1
SELECT * FROM student WHERE department_id=1;   -- N times
```

**Lazy is not the enemy.** Missing a fetch plan for a known use case is.

Switching mapping to `EAGER` is a blunt fix: loads association even when unused, and may still use extra selects.

***

## Topic 4 — Detect with SQL logging

```properties
spring.jpa.show-sql=true
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true
logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=DEBUG
```

Run the loop. Count statements. If you see repeats inside a for-loop, you found N+1.

***

## Topic 5 — Fix with EntityGraph (query-level plan)

Keep mapping lazy. Tell **this** repository method what to fetch.

```java
public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> {

    @EntityGraph(attributePaths = "department")
    List<Student> findAll();
}
```

```text
Default mapping: department LAZY
This method:     Student + Department in one fetch plan
```

Multiple / nested:

```java
@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"department", "profile"})
List<Student> findAll();

@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"department.manager"})
List<Student> findAll();
```

Other tools (same idea): JPQL `join fetch`, batch fetching. Prefer **lazy default + explicit plan**.

***

## Practice lab

1. `@ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY)` on `Student.department`.  
2. `findAll` students; loop print department names; count SQL.  
3. Add `@EntityGraph(attributePaths = "department")` on a query method.  
4. Repeat loop; SQL count should drop.  
5. Add `cascade = PERSIST` on `Order.items`; persist order with two new items in one call.  
6. Confirm cascade ≠ ownership: only setting inverse collection without owning FK still fails.

***

## Short map to keep

```text
Cascade:  parent op → child ops (lifecycle)
Lazy:     load later when touched
N+1:      1 + N hidden queries in a loop
Fix:      EntityGraph / join fetch per use case
```
